title: Ishan Kishan Rises to World No.1 in T20I Rankings Ahead of England Series — Only the Fourth Indian to Reach the Summit
excerpt: The wicketkeeper-batter overtakes teammate Abhishek Sharma in the latest ICC update, capping a remarkable comeback from a two-year exile
body:
India's Ishan Kishan has reached the pinnacle of T20 international cricket. In the latest ICC Men's T20I Player Rankings update released on Tuesday, the 27-year-old left-hander overtook teammate Abhishek Sharma to become the world's No.1-ranked T20I batter — making him only the fourth Indian to achieve the feat after Virat Kohli, Suryakumar Yadav, and Sharma himself.

The changing of the guard at the top was a matter of when, not if. Kishan had been trailing Sharma by a razor-thin four rating points — 871 to 875 — since the conclusion of the T20 World Cup in March. But Sharma has not played international cricket since March 9, when he smashed a 21-ball half-century in the World Cup final against New Zealand. The weekly rankings algorithm penalises inactivity, and Sharma's three-month absence from international duty, combined with his exclusion from India's touring squads, has finally seen his points erode enough for Kishan to leapfrog him.

## A Comeback for the Ages

What makes Kishan's ascent especially remarkable is the journey that preceded it. In late 2023, the wicketkeeper-batter stepped away from cricket entirely, citing mental fatigue and the toll of being repeatedly benched despite strong domestic performances. His father later confirmed that Kishan had been "very depressed" during that period. The cricketer turned to spirituality and the Bhagavad Gita for solace, using the break to rebuild both his technique and his mental fortitude.

When Kishan returned to the Indian setup in January 2026 for the home T20I series against New Zealand, he had been away for 785 days. He wasted little time making up for lost ground. A blistering 76 off 32 balls in the second T20I at Raipur — including a 21-ball half-century — announced his return in emphatic fashion. He followed that with a maiden T20I century in the fifth match, smashing 103 off 43 balls.

## World Cup Hero

Kishan's resurgence peaked at the T20 World Cup 2026, where he was one of India's most impactful performers. He amassed 317 runs across the tournament, including a match-winning 77 off 40 balls against Pakistan in Colombo and 61 off 24 balls against Namibia — the latter making him the first Indian wicketkeeper to score a half-century in T20 World Cup history. His consistent contributions were instrumental in India lifting the trophy.

The World Cup campaign vaulted Kishan from eighth in the rankings to second, just four points behind Sharma. Since then, while Sharma sat out of India's squads, Kishan continued to feature. He was part of India's squad for the Ireland T20I series last week, though the team suffered a shocking 2-0 clean sweep at the hands of the hosts — India's first bilateral series loss to an Associate nation in the format.

## Timing Is Everything

The No.1 ranking arrives at an opportune moment. India begin a five-match T20I series against England today at the Riverside Ground in Chester-le-Street, with Kishan set to bat in his first match as the world's top-ranked T20I batter. The series is a chance for redemption after the Ireland embarrassment, and for Kishan personally, a stage to cement his place at the summit.

<instagram url="https://www.instagram.com/p/DaPkj0vjLrX/" />

Shreyas Iyer leads the Indian side in the absence of several senior players, with Kishan, Tilak Varma, and Sanju Samson forming the batting core. England, captained by Harry Brook, will be without Jofra Archer for the series opener.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora across the UK, the timing could not be better. An Indian batter atop the world rankings, playing a high-profile series on English soil, offers NRI cricket fans a compelling reason to tune in — or head to the ground. Kishan's story of resilience, mental health recovery, and cricketing redemption resonates beyond the boundary rope, mirroring the persistence and reinvention that defines so many diaspora journeys.

The last time two batters from the same nation held the top two T20I spots was Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan of Pakistan in September 2022. With Kishan now ahead and Sharma still nominally at No.2, India's dominance of the format's batting hierarchy remains intact — even as the team searches for answers after its Irish misadventure.

Kishan's rise to the summit is a testament to the power of second chances. From the depths of a mental health crisis to the top of the world: few comebacks in modern cricket have been quite this complete.
